research_brief.research_summary: A log ladder upward in kilograms: you, a blue whale, the Eiffel Tower, all of humanity, Earth, the Sun and a neutron star, the Milky Way's black hole, then a break to the observable universe's ordinary matter; dark matter outweighs it about five to one.

data_points.claim: Blue whale: largest animal; adults commonly ~100-150 t, largest weighed ~190 t. PROBABLY ('can reach a hundred and fifty thousand' kg) [WHALE]
Eiffel Tower total 10,100 t (metal frame 7,300 t) = ~10 million kg. MEASURED [EIFFEL]
All humans combined: estimates 287-390 million t (2005-2018 studies); ~8 billion x ~65 kg = ~520 million t; 'around four hundred billion kg'. PROBABLY [HUMANITY]
data_points.source_name: Yale e360 (Bar-On et al. 2018) / BMC Public Health 2012

data_points.claim: Neutron star: typically ~1.4 solar masses in a sphere ~20 km across (city-sized). MEASURED (typical) [NEUTRON]
Sagittarius A*: ~4 million solar masses (~8e36 kg); its event horizon (~24 million km across) would fit well inside Mercury's orbit (~116 million km across). MEASURED [SGRA]
Ordinary (baryonic) matter in the observable universe ~1.5e53 kg (critical density x Omega_b 0.0485 x volume). PROBABLY (an estimate) [UNIVERSE]
Dark matter outweighs ordinary matter ~5.4 to 1 (Omega_c 0.265 vs Omega_b 0.049, Planck 2018). PROBABLY (inferred, not directly detected) [DARK]

1.5e53 kg written out has 53 zeros before the decimal point... counted as digits after the leading 15: 1.5e53 = 15 followed by 52 zeros; the ZEROS counter counts powers of ten (53). MEASURED (arithmetic) [ZEROS]
